extra.message: acct_shell_probe_399() builds a shell command by concatenating the unsanitized 'host' GET parameter directly into os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). A value like '127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd' or '$(id)' is passed straight to the shell, giving arbitrary OS command execution.

acct_jinja_cast_381() takes the 'fragment' GET parameter and renders it directly as a Jinja2 template via Template("Result: " + fragment).render(). An attacker can supply Jinja2 syntax (e.g. {{ self.__init__.__globals__.__builtins__.__import__('os').popen('id').read() }}) to achieve server-side template injection and remote code execution.

acct_xml_fold_451() parses request.body with etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) and feeds it to etree.fromstring(). This configuration explicitly enables DTD loading, external entity resolution, and network access, allowing a crafted XML payload with a DOCTYPE/ENTITY to read local files or perform SSRF via XXE.

acct_packet_pull_002() joins the unsanitized 'packet_ref' GET parameter directly onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR and reads it with Path.read_text(). A value like '../../../../etc/passwd' escapes the intended directory and reads arbitrary files on the server's filesystem.

acct_dock_shelf_388() joins the unsanitized 'name' GET parameter onto BASE_EXPORT_DIR and writes the raw request body to that path via Path.write_bytes(). A value like '../../../../var/www/app/shell.py' or an absolute path allows writing arbitrary files anywhere the process can write, including overwriting application code.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: acct_vault_stash_233() builds a file path from the unsanitized 'ref' GET parameter (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json') and writes attacker-supplied SSN and card-number values to it in cleartext. 'ref' can contain '../' to write outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR, and the SSN/card data is persisted unencrypted to disk.

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: acct_vendor_ping_003() passes the unvalidated 'url' GET parameter directly to urllib.request.urlopen(). An attacker can point this at internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or internal admin endpoints), making the server fetch and return internal-only content — classic SSRF.

acct_identity_ping_333() is the only handler in this module that does not call _wrk_gate(request) before processing the request. Every sibling endpoint requires the 'x-internal-token' header to match INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN; this one is reachable by any unauthenticated caller, allowing anyone to queue an identity 'ping' for an arbitrary handle/channel.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: acct_badge_gate_439() grants an elevated privilege lane (full payroll/casework access) whenever the client-supplied cookie 'ops_badge' or header 'x-ops-badge' equals the hardcoded literal string 'lead'. Since the client fully controls this cookie/header, any caller who passes the gate check can set it to escalate privileges — an authorization decision based entirely on client-supplied, hardcoded value.

acct_identity_hint_359() checks a caller-supplied 'verifier' against hardcoded secrets in the 'known' dict using '!=' (a non-constant-time comparison), enabling a timing side-channel to recover the 4-digit verifier byte-by-byte, in addition to the secrets themselves being hardcoded in source.

acct_origin_mirror_369() reflects the caller-supplied Origin header back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin and also sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This lets any origin make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the response, defeating same-origin protections (CORS misconfiguration).

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: acct_return_lane_149() redirects to the raw 'lane' value taken from GET/POST with no validation of scheme or host. An attacker-supplied absolute URL (e.g. //evil.example.com/) causes the server to issue an open redirect, usable for phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site (Open Redirect)

extra.message: acct_workset_rebind_191() merges the entire caller-controlled JSON body into a security-relevant dict via workset.update(payload), letting the caller directly set protected fields like 'role', 'approved', and 'tier' without any allow-list — a mass-assignment vulnerability that lets a low-privilege caller flip 'approved' to true or 'role' to an elevated value.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: acct_delta_121() trusts the client-supplied 'amount' and 'state' values directly, including setting ledger['state'] from user input (defaulting to 'approved' if unspecified). A caller can set state=approved (or any value) regardless of actual approval logic, effectively self-approving a ledger transaction.

acct_trust_drift_429() creates an SSL context with ssl._create_unverified_context() and uses it for an outbound HTTPS request, disabling certificate validation and hostname verification. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks against the outbound connection.
acct_frame_slip_419() explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and clears the Content-Security-Policy header on the response, disabling browser-side XSS mitigations for that response.

acct_digest_fold_273() uses hashlib.md5() to digest a caller-supplied 'phrase'. MD5 is cryptographically broken; if this digest is used for any integrity or identification purpose it is trivially forgeable/collidable.

acct_nonce_roll_409() uses the non-cryptographic random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) to build a 'code' value that is returned to the caller as a nonce. If this code is used for any security purpose (auth code, token), it is predictable and should use the 'secrets' module instead.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message:
The 'safe_break' template filter calls mark_safe() on the input after only replacing newlines with
, without HTML-escaping the rest of the string. It is applied in templates directly to user-controlled, persisted TextFields — e.g. EscalationComment.body (templates/escalations/detail.html:76 and templates/customer_portal/escalation_detail.html:28, populated via EscalationCommentForm.save() in crm/forms.py from both staff and customer-contact input in crm/views/customer_portal.py escalation_reply), as well as Escalation.customer_summary/internal_summary and Deal.notes and Organization.notes. Any HTML/JS in these fields (e.g. a comment body of '' posted by a customer contact via the portal reply form) is rendered unescaped to every other viewer of that escalation, resulting in stored XSS.

WebhookForm.clean_target_url() validates the hostname string at form-submission time against a blocklist of literal private/loopback IPs and reserved hostnames, but the actual outbound request in crm/views/webhooks.py test_delivery() (urllib.request.urlopen(req)) resolves and connects to the hostname again at delivery time. Because validation and connection are two separate steps (TOCTOU), an attacker who controls DNS for the target hostname (or uses a rebinding service) can pass validation with a public-looking domain that later resolves to 127.0.0.1 or a cloud metadata IP (169.254.169.254), bypassing the SSRF blocklist when ENABLE_REAL_WEBHOOK_DELIVERY is enabled.

DEBUG defaults to True (_env_bool("DJANGO_DEBUG", default=True)) unless DJANGO_DEBUG is explicitly set in the environment. If a production deployment forgets to set this variable, Django will render detailed tracebacks (including settings, SQL, and local variables) to any visitor who triggers a 500 error, leaking sensitive internal information.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
